The other committed deltas are S1's own oracle and support (tests/acceptance/review_app_scan_store_failure.rs, and the +14 purely additive lines in support/review_app/app.rs: TEST_FAULT_VAR and restart_without_test_fault, which nothing in S2's oracle calls) and the user's unrelated cleanup 03c4a71. The execution recorded in R1 is a new one, taken after this comparison, not a replay of either.

Semantic RED, not infrastructure: the target compiles and collects (5 tests run, 0 filtered). The single failure is the promised observation missing from production, panicking at tests/acceptance/review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs:109:9 inside then_her_queue_says_nothing_about_repos_read with 'WHAT: her queue says "repos read" for a run kept before any scan plan was stored', and the captured page shows the real defect verbatim ('10 new suggestions 0 repos read 8 pending'). No import error, no missing fixture, no cross-root path mismatch, no provider mismatch. The two control scenarios pass on pre-fix production, which is correct: they protect behaviour that already exists.

E4 closure (completed run with no planned repos shows no repos-read line at all, not a zero or placeholder): falsified by a_run_kept_before_scan_plans_were_stored_says_nothing_about_repos_read, which asserts the whole queue text holds neither 'repos read' nor 'repo read', so a zero count and any count-shaped placeholder both fail. The declared absence carries its discriminator rather than passing vacuously: then_it_is_a_finished_scans_queue pins the page as a completed run's queue ('Scan again' offered, 'new suggestion' present) and then_her_suggestions_are_the_kept_ones pins it to the kept data, so an error page, a signed-out page or a queue with no run cannot satisfy the absence.

E5 closure (a completed run that had planned repos keeps its line, with the true number of repos read): falsified by a_scan_that_read_the_repos_it_planned_says_how_many (5 planned, 5 read, '5 repos read') and a_scan_that_could_read_none_of_the_repos_it_planned_still_says_so (1 planned, 0 read, '0 repos read'). The expected count is not fabricated by the test and not re-read from the page under assertion: given_scanned returns repos_read_since, computed from the hermetic GitHub double's own HTTP request log (support/review_app/repos_and_accounts.rs:1020, paths /repos/{owner}/{name}/...). The oracle is therefore independent of the production count logic and would not pass with that logic deleted.

The three scenarios discriminate the promised rule from the two plausible wrong rules, exactly as acceptance.md's per-row falsifiers claim. 'Hide the line whenever the count is nought' is rejected by the planned-run-that-read-nothing scenario, which demands '0 repos read' and names 'Skipped priyaraman/kelp: archived since you chose it' as the only public sign that the run holds a plan row for kelp. 'Keep the line for every completed run' is rejected by the plan-less-run scenario. 'Report planned repos instead of repos read' is also rejected by the archived-repo scenario, where planned is 1 and read is 0; the five-repo scenario alone could not tell those apart, and acceptance.md records that honestly.

Driving port and contract shape are honest. Every scenario drives the real review-app binary's public HTTP page /review through the JS-less browser double (scan_summary -> browser.open("/review").text()); no private module, domain object or store handle is reached, and the file's own header states that nothing in it opens the app's store. The @real-io tag matches the composition it actually drives: the app's real on-disk DuckDB store is live, while GitHub and the ATProto network are hermetic capturing doubles, which is the Architecture-of-Reference treatment for a driven-internal store and driven-external dependencies.

Constructible before craft, with a faithful GIVEN. Every helper the oracle calls exists in the declared support surface at the reviewed bytes (rra_world_on_v1_store, v1_golden_pending, given_scanned/repos_read_since, scan_summary, pending_on_queue, given_signed_in, given_owner_verified, given_saved_choice, github.archive_repo), and Cargo.toml carries the [[test]] block naming the target. The plan-less GIVEN is faithful rather than asserted into existence: tests/fixtures/review-app-store-v1/README.md records a store frozen at schema v1 on 2026-10-19, written by the release before the ADR-088 v2 migration added the scan-plan tables, holding a completed run that read five repos but no plan row for any of them.

No existing observation contradicts what this oracle demands, so the fix cannot be blocked by a conflicting incumbent test. Every other assertion of the line is for a run that has a plan (review_app_repos_and_accounts.rs:434 formats 'N repos read' for the planned set; review_app_repos_and_accounts_imports.rs:365 asserts 'No GitHub account to re-check - 1 repo read'). The two scenarios that open the queue on the same frozen v1 store never assert the line: MG-1 compares pending cards and backups, and MG-2's state-delta universe (capture_rra) captures pds claims, pending cards, not-yours cards, accounts and imports, never the summary text. review_app_lifecycle.rs:52-56 asserts only the summary segments '1 new', '3 already published', '1 declined (hidden)' by containment, on a current-release scan that has plan rows.

typesafe: unavailable. The reviewer-owned batch (E4/E5 closure, absence discriminator, oracle independence, hide-on-zero discrimination, residual-gap classification, constructibility) was submitted to the installed client as scripts/jev_decide.py --request - --output - from a shell command with no file written; it exited 3 reporting TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent, and the key is absent from a login shell too. No call was fabricated and no producer-owned judgment was consumed; every judgment recorded here is my own, verified against the reviewed oracle bytes, the authority documents and my own measured run.

Residual limits, recorded rather than charged as defects. (1) No scenario anywhere runs a NEW planned scan on a store migrated from the plan-less release, so an implementation keying the hidden line on store provenance instead of plan rows would pass; plausibility is low, since no provenance column exists and the architecture states the rule as 'no scan_run_repos rows'. (2) The target also runs two support unit tests (review_app::state_delta::tests::*) pulled in by the #[path] support module, a pre-existing convention of every suite in this crate, not an S2 artefact. (3) repos_read_line and REPOS_READ_WORDINGS are declared identically in this oracle and in S1's review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:57-58,217-218; the shared home for that wording is support/review_app/, which S2 does not declare as a support, so folding it there is best done when a slice next amends that support.

Test time: no budget statement or per-test measurement is required here and none is claimed. The whole target, three real-io scenarios each launching the real binary plus the two support unit tests, finished in 2.76 s wall on the clean-HEAD run (7.93 s on my earlier run, 3.43 s on the root's), nowhere near a half-budget or derogation threshold, so no nine-run median was taken.

diagnostic: Accepted, no findings. The oracle is public, independent and complete for P2 as selected: it drives only the real binary's /review page, and both closure directions hold. E4 is falsified by the plan-less-run scenario, whose absence claim carries its own discriminator (the page is pinned as a completed run's queue showing the kept suggestions), and E5 by the two planned-run scenarios, whose expected count comes from the GitHub double's request log rather than from the page being asserted. The archived-repo scenario is what makes the pair discriminating: it rejects both 'hide whenever the count is nought' and 'report planned instead of read'. Criteria adequacy was checked before the oracle: the selected criteria preserve the user decision of 2026-11-08 and lose no promised outcome, and the plan-less GIVEN is faithful to the frozen schema-v1 fixture rather than assumed. Semantic RED is measured and mine, taken on clean HEAD ef5f6e5 whose S2 oracle bytes and [[test]] block are identical to the reviewed b8de1e9: exit 101, one failure at review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs:109:9 on the missing promised observation with the real page quoted, the two controls passing; it is not an import, fixture or collection defect. Craft may start. Completion still owes implementation GREEN on all three scenarios; the three residual limits in R11 are advisory and veto nothing.
